name: Calyptocarpus

project_scope.note: Genus recognition focused on documented local C. vialis. Do not assume every trait below is invariant across all Calyptocarpus taxa worldwide.

look_here_first: Small opposite, shallow-toothed leaves on prostrate branches; tiny yellow composite heads nearly sessile in leaf axils. Confirm actual ray + disc florets and green overlapping phyllaries; mature fruits bear conspicuous awns.

shared_traits: Asteraceae: inflorescence is a compact HEAD of many tiny florets, not one ordinary flower.
Plants typically small and spreading/procumbent; leaves opposite, petiolate, shallowly toothed.
Tiny axillary yellow-rayed heads, often on very short stalks.
Dry one-seeded cypselae bear prominent awns of the pappus; close-up is more dependable than flower color alone.
shared_genus_recognition.caution: Specific head dimensions, leaf length and pappus counts here are documented primarily for C. vialis in Central Texas; check other Calyptocarpus species with a flora before assigning exact measurements.

study_strategy.look_here_first: Follow the shoot to a node: leaf pair → axillary capitulum → phyllaries beneath head → mature awned cypsela.
shared_traits: Small opposite petiolate leaves with toothed margins and low, often creeping branch architecture.
Axillary composite flower heads with short yellow ray florets and yellow disc florets.
Green involucral phyllaries surrounding head and mature cypsela with barbed pappus awns.
priority: 01 Habit: prostrate or low ascending, with creeping branches through turf.
02 Node: opposite paired leaves, short petioles, shallow teeth and small leaf veins.
03 Head: find a yellow ray-and-disc capitulum nestled in the leaf axil (not an elongate frogfruit button).
04 Confirm: magnify phyllaries beneath the head and barbed awns of a mature cypsela.
05 Look-alike check: distinguish low unrelated mats and coarser yellow Asteraceae.
study_strategy.warning: A tiny yellow flower is not enough. Many plants creep or have opposite leaves; check the actual composite head and its axillary placement. Three-angled cypselae are variable, so never make three angles a mandatory character.

genus_diagnostics.habit: C. vialis is a low perennial branching/procumbent or prostrate herb with short strigose hairs.
genus_diagnostics.leaf_arrangement: Opposite, often decussate, simple, petiolate and shallowly toothed.
genus_diagnostics.inflorescence: Capitulum, typically solitary, axillary, short-peduncled to subsessile; yellow outer ray florets and yellow inner disc florets.
genus_diagnostics.phyllaries: Small overlapping involucral bracts (approximately four to six reported in local detailed treatment).
genus_diagnostics.fruit: Dry flattened cypselae typically with two conspicuous barbed pappus awns, with smaller supplemental awns possible.

quick_key.if: Tiny flowers packed into a button or short cylinder, conspicuously raised on a naked stalk
Kidney/coin-shaped entire leaf blades; no yellow ray-and-disc composite head
Small white-rayed composite head with slender opposite leaves, especially damp sites
Larger yellow/orange heads on long stalks, coarser rough foliage and taller perennial stems
Tiny yellow heads crowded in leaf axils, low mat; opposite small toothed leaves and barbed cypsela awns

comparison_cards.title: Straggler daisy vs frogfruit
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Compare the FLOWER HEAD first: tiny yellow ray-and-disc capitulum vs dense pale button of individual verbena-type flowers.

field_matrix.straggler_daisy: Yellow ray + tubular disc florets in tiny daisy-like head
field_matrix.frogfruit: Numerous small whitish/lavender flowers densely packed into a button/cylinder

comparison_cards.caution: Without flowers, examine a full mature shoot and several leaves; do not force species ID from a single damaged leaf.

comparison_cards.title: Straggler daisy vs Carolina ponyfoot
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Read the leaves: two opposite toothed leaves vs alternate, round/kidney-shaped entire leaves on conspicuous petioles.

field_matrix.ponyfoot: Reniform (kidney) or round, smooth margin, alternate

comparison_cards.title: Straggler daisy vs false daisy (Eclipta)
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Both have opposite foliage and small composite heads; check WHITE vs YELLOW rays, leaf blade shape and wet-ground association.

field_matrix.straggler_daisy: Often drier lawn edges and general disturbed ground

comparison_cards.title: Straggler daisy vs hairy wedelia
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Do not rely on yellow. Compare actual HEAD SIZE, length of flower stalk and mature growth habit.

field_matrix.wedelia: Conspicuous larger golden-yellow/orange daisy heads on long peduncles
Coarser perennial/subshrub often woody at base
field_matrix.strength: high except repeatedly mowed juvenile material

diagnostic_photo_requirements.role: Shoot with opposite leaf pairs and short-toothed blades
Axillary yellow capitulum face and side view with neighboring leaf node
Green phyllaries beneath head (side/underside) with scale
Mature cypsela with pappus awns and mm scale
Matched side-by-side photo of Calyptocarpus vs Phyla vs Eclipta
